title: Ability Audit Event
description: One recorded attempt to invoke a WordPress ability. Emitted from wp_ability_invoked, which fires before the permission check and before input validation — so an event proves a caller asked, never that the call was permitted, valid, or executed.

event_id.description: Unique identity. Redelivery MUST be idempotent on this value.

correlation_id.description: Groups the phases of one attempt. Never reused, and stable when one ability invokes another.

ability_name.description: Namespaced ability name. A recorder MUST ignore names outside its own namespace: wp_ability_invoked is global, so an unfiltered recorder double-counts every other plugin's invocations.

actor_ref.description: Opaque caller reference. MUST NOT be an email address, login name, or other directly identifying value.

validation_outcome.description: Two-phase. Written 'pending' at invocation and resolved when wp_ability_validate_input reports. Still 'pending' at delivery means validation never reported — a real outcome, which MUST NOT be rewritten.

summary.description: The ONLY representation of ability input permitted to leave memory. Raw input is never stored in any form.

type.description: PHP type of the input, nothing more.

bytes.description: Byte length of the input's JSON encoding. Size distinguishes a normal call from an attempt to flood the audit path.

digest.description: Keyed hash of the JSON encoding, using a site-local secret that is never itself recorded. MUST NOT be a bare hash: an unkeyed digest of a short or low-entropy input is reversible by brute force.

shape.description: Recursive structure with every value removed, bounded in depth and breadth. Key names are retained as the diagnostic content, except where a key is itself sensitive.

redaction.description: Human-readable statement of the guarantee, so an operator reading a stored row can see what it does and does not hold.
